claims.text: Wear resistance of the Al-containing HEA coating will improve as temperature increases up to a critical boundary because a protective oxide layer forms.
The improvement in tribological performance will persist from ambient temperature to approximately 400-500 °C.
Beyond the critical temperature, oxide instability or matrix softening will degrade tribological performance.
An AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 or similar Al-containing coating deposited by laser cladding or sputtering will have a solid-solution or multiphase microstructure with high hardness.
Elevated-temperature sliding will produce a continuous, adherent, hard oxide scale on the coating.
The protective oxide scale will consist of oxides such as Al2O3 and Cr2O3.
Elevated temperature increases the diffusion rates of Al and Cr.
Faster Al and Cr diffusion facilitates rapid formation of the protective oxide layer.
The protective oxide layer acts as a solid lubricant, lowers the coefficient of friction, and separates the sliding surfaces.
Separation by the oxide layer minimizes adhesive and abrasive wear.
Bulk AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 exhibits increased elevated-temperature wear resistance due to formation of a protective oxide layer.
Bulk AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 exhibits a slight decrease in coefficient of friction with increasing temperature.
The bulk-alloy mechanism transfers to a coating because surface chemistry and oxidation kinetics dominate the response.
Wear rate will decrease by approximately 30-50% between 25 °C and 400 °C.
Coefficient of friction will decrease by approximately 10-20% between 25 °C and 400 °C.
Above 500 °C, wear rate may increase because of oxide spallation or matrix softening, and coefficient of friction may rise.
The degradation boundary depends on alloy composition, refractory-element content, and coating-substrate interface stability.
A similar or greater wear-resistance improvement in the Al-free control, or absence of oxide and wear improvement in the Al-containing coating, would falsify the proposed Al-induced oxide mechanism.

contradictions.description: The critical boundary is stated inconsistently: the hypothesis places it at approximately 400-500 °C, the predicted outcome places degradation above 500 °C, and the boundary field places it above 500-600 °C.
